q: Does the lime a Moroccan EAF mill buys count in its CBAM figure?
title: EAF mills: bought lime in the CBAM figure
short: Bought burnt lime does not add CO2 to your direct emissions: it was calcined at the lime plant, and lime is not a CBAM precursor for steel. Only limestone or raw dolomite charged into your own furnace releases process CO2 at your site, and that counts.
audience: Electric arc furnace steel mills in Morocco and North Africa that buy quicklime or dolomitic lime for slag practice

ul: Quicklime or calcined dolomite bought in: no process CO2 at your mill. Record the tonnes anyway, because the verifier checks the slag balance.
Raw limestone or dolomite charged into the furnace: CO2 released in your furnace. Use tonnes charged times the stoichiometric factor, 0.440 t CO2 per tonne of calcium carbonate, adjusted for purity.

sections.h: Why lime is not a precursor
p: For iron and steel goods, the relevant precursors are crude steel, pig iron, DRI and the covered ferro alloys. Lime is not a CBAM good, so its upstream calcination stays with the lime maker and out of your embedded emissions.
Lime is still a purchased good in your Scope 3. An EU buyer asking for a full product footprint, beyond CBAM, may want it, so keep the lime supplier's figure if you can get one.

example.title: Illustrative carbonate CO2 for one month
lines: Raw dolomite charged: 120 t at 95% carbonate
Process CO2: 120 x 0.95 x 0.477 = 54.4 t CO2 (dolomite factor 0.477 t CO2 per tonne)
Quicklime bought: 900 t, no process CO2 at this mill
example.note: Quantities are illustrative. Use your own charge records and the carbonate content from the supplier analysis.
